analysis.title: GS ETF Color - charts & bullets...
key_insights: NDX fell 3.4% on the last day of October, a two standard deviation daily move, finishing its worst month of the year. The broader market is still up double digits year to date.
US-listed ETFs took in just over $200B in October, the second-largest monthly inflow in GS's dataset. Year-to-date inflows are +$1.7T.

In October, ETFs that underperformed NDX saw larger inflows as a percentage of their asset base. Within non-levered equity ETFs, semis took the most inflows, followed by broad-based tech, EM and Brazil-exposed ETFs.
Levered ETFs had their largest month of inflows in the dataset, +$13B in assets.
On Friday alone levered ETFs took in +$3B, the group's largest daily inflow year to date.
Historically, levered ETF flows are strongest on -2σ market days and weakest on +2σ days, which is consistent with the October and Friday inflows.
NDX had its largest monthly underperformance versus equal-weight SPX since 2002.
Health care rose about 10% in October, its best month since April 2020. XLV took in +$1.6B, its best monthly inflow since May 2022.
The desk faced supply for miners on Friday. COPX has fallen for 10 consecutive weeks, tying the longest weekly losing streak since the fund launched in 2010.
risk_factors: The trading environment has become more complex despite double-digit year-to-date gains in the broader market.
NDX had its worst month of the year and its largest underperformance versus equal-weight SPX since 2002.
vol_and_positioning: Levered ETFs took in +$13B in October, a record month, and +$3B on Friday, the largest daily inflow year to date. Flows into the group are historically strongest on -2σ days and weakest on +2σ days.
NDX's -3.4% move on Friday was a two standard deviation daily move.
Non-levered ETFs that underperformed NDX in October saw larger inflows relative to assets, led by semis, broad tech, EM and Brazil.
